docs.title: pytest-fastprom
docs.text:
Proof of concept

This project is a proof of concept. The approach still needs real-world feedback (REX) before it can be considered validated, so treat results as a signal, not a guarantee. Most of the code was generated using generative AI.

docs.title: Why this project
docs.text:
pytest-fastprom started as a proof of concept around a specific blind spot: performance regressions you can't see in a code review.

The kind of change that looks harmless in a diff but quietly costs you milliseconds at runtime:

  • an ORM relationship that now triggers an N+1 or a cache-busting join,
  • a new middleware that runs on every request,
  • an algorithm swapped for one with worse complexity on real-world input.

None of these break a test. None of them show up until latency creeps into production. The idea here is to catch those drawbacks early, right in the test suite, by reusing the measurement tool your app already trusts: Prometheus.

Not a load-testing tool

This is not a replacement for real load testing. Reach for k6 or Locust when you need concurrency, sustained throughput, or production-scale traffic.

`pytest-fastprom` aims for something narrower and faster: a quick signal, on every test run, that a change didn't silently regress the latency or error budget you promised, measured with the same Prometheus histograms you already ship.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
uv add --dev pytest-fastprom
# or
pip install pytest-fastprom

docs.title: Marker reference
docs.text:
@pytest.mark.metrics(...) accepts:

kwarg meaning handler, method scope assertions to one path / HTTP method p50_below, p99_below latency percentile < threshold (seconds) min_requests total request count >= N no_errors zero 5xx responses max_error_rate 5xx rate <= fraction (e.g. 0.01 = 1%) max_4xx_rate 4xx rate <= fraction warmup_rounds, warmup_url run N warmup requests first, excluded from the window

docs.title: Regression detection
docs.text:
# record a baseline (stores metrics + git commit + machine info)
pytest --metrics-save=main

# later, fail the build if latency drifts past the threshold
pytest --metrics-compare=main --metrics-compare-fail='p50:10%,p99:20%'

When the baseline was recorded on a different interpreter or architecture, the comparison still runs but prints a warning so you don't trust a cross-machine delta.

docs.title: Assert against your SLO
docs.text:
Drive the app through instrumented_client, then assert on the metrics fixture:

def test_home_meets_slo(instrumented_client, metrics):
    instrumented_client.get("/")
    metrics.assert_p99_below(1.0, handler="/")
    metrics.assert_no_server_errors()

docs.title: Declare the SLO on the test
docs.text:
The metrics marker checks the budget after the test body runs:

@pytest.mark.metrics(p99_below=1.0, min_requests=3, no_errors=True)
def test_route_within_budget(instrumented_client):
    for _ in range(3):
        instrumented_client.get("/")

docs.title: Spend an error budget
docs.text:
Allow a ratio of failures instead of demanding zero:

@pytest.mark.metrics(handler="/checkout", max_error_rate=0.01, max_4xx_rate=0.05)
def test_checkout_stays_in_budget(instrumented_client):
    for _ in range(100):
        instrumented_client.post("/checkout")
    # passes while 5xx <= 1% and 4xx <= 5% of requests

docs.title: Assert on your own metrics
docs.text:
Declare a metric the ordinary way (a module-level Counter on the default registry) and assert without any wiring:

# in your app
from prometheus_client import Counter
CACHE_HITS = Counter("cache_hits", "served from cache", ["region"])

# in your test
def test_cache_is_used(instrumented_client, metrics):
    instrumented_client.get("/items/1")
    metrics.assert_metric("cache_hits_total", at_least=1)          # this test's delta
    metrics.assert_metric("queue_depth", delta=False, at_most=10)  # gauge: absolute

labels is a subset filter (omit it to sum every series). Because the app's global registry is shared across tests, counters report this test's delta by default; pass delta=False for a gauge whose current value you want as-is.
